# Practical coding

English · [Русский](../ru/themes/coding-practical.md) · ← [AI Interview Atlas](../../README.md)

Work-like coding: concurrency, rate limits, retries, evolving specifications, debugging and code review.

## Both tracks

- **Refactor a small, poorly structured program with passing tests. Explain the first change and how you preserve observable behaviour.**
  - Coding · Asked at: [OpenAI](../companies/openai.md) †
  - Tests: Whether improvements are incremental and justified by maintainability.

## AI Engineering

- **Implement scaled dot-product attention with a causal mask and tests that would expose attention to future tokens.**
  - Coding · Asked at: [Amazon](../companies/amazon.md) †, [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) †, [Google and Google DeepMind](../companies/google.md) †
  - Tests: Whether shapes, masking and numerical stability are correct in executable code.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Check batch, sequence and head dimensions before implementing score multiplication.
    - Use stable softmax after masking disallowed positions.
    - Test small hand-computable cases and ensure changing future inputs cannot change earlier outputs.
  - Read: [Attention Is All You Need](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762) (Vaswani et al., arXiv)
- **Implement multi-head attention, then modify the implementation so several query heads share each pair of key and value heads.**
  - Coding · Asked at: [Google and Google DeepMind](../companies/google.md) †
  - Tests: Whether tensor layout and head grouping are implemented consistently.
- **Implement one-token decoding with a KV cache and compare its output with a full-prefix forward pass.**
  - Coding
  - Tests: Whether positions, cache updates and attention masks remain correct.
- **Write a small BPE trainer and encoder, specifying how merge ties and unseen input symbols are handled.**
  - Coding
  - Tests: Whether learned merges and encoding behaviour agree.
- **Implement temperature scaling, top-k filtering and nucleus sampling for a logits vector, including boundary cases.**
  - Coding · Asked at: [Google and Google DeepMind](../companies/google.md) †
  - Tests: Whether probability mass, ties and invalid parameters are handled correctly.
- **Build a cache with constant-time lookup and recency updates, then add expiry without breaking eviction semantics.**
  - Coding · Asked at: [OpenAI](../companies/openai.md) †
  - Tests: Whether data-structure invariants survive an evolving specification.
- **Implement a token-bucket limiter and explain what must change when several workers enforce the same limit.**
  - Coding · Asked at: [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) †, [OpenAI](../companies/openai.md) †
  - Tests: Whether time accounting and concurrent updates preserve the quota.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Refill from elapsed monotonic time and cap tokens at capacity.
    - Make the check-and-consume operation atomic across competing calls.
    - Test bursts and time boundaries; state the shared-store or partitioning contract for distributed enforcement.
  - Read: [Scaling your API with rate limiters](https://stripe.com/blog/rate-limiters) (Stripe)
- **Write an asynchronous API batch processor with bounded concurrency, retry jitter and isolated per-item failures.**
  - Coding · Asked at: [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) †, [Perplexity](../companies/perplexity.md) †
  - Tests: Whether cancellation, retries and results remain well-defined under partial failure.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Bound in-flight work and propagate cancellation and deadlines.
    - Retry only suitable failures with capped backoff and jitter; consider idempotency.
    - Return per-item outcomes and test timeouts, permanent failures and partial completion.
  - Read: [Designing robust and predictable APIs with idempotency](https://stripe.com/blog/idempotency) (Stripe) · [Site Reliability Engineering](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/) (Google)
- **Implement an incremental SSE parser whose data events can contain JSON split across arbitrary network chunks.**
  - Coding
  - Tests: Whether transport boundaries are kept separate from message boundaries.
- **Implement overlapping text chunks that preserve semantic units; define what happens when one unit exceeds the target size.**
  - Coding
  - Tests: Whether ambiguous size and boundary requirements are clarified before coding.
- **Implement exact cosine similarity search over embeddings and explain the limits that would require a different production design.**
  - Coding
  - Tests: Whether a correct baseline is separated from a scalable serving system.
- **Implement a minimal agent runner with validated tool dispatch, error handling and a hard step limit.**
  - Coding
  - Tests: Whether loop state and terminal conditions are explicit in code.
- **Implement an in-memory key-value store with begin, commit and abort, stating the transaction semantics you support.**
  - Coding · Asked at: [OpenAI](../companies/openai.md) †
  - Tests: Whether rollback and visibility match a precise contract.
- **Write a function that collects a paginated REST result while handling page size, termination and incomplete responses explicitly.**
  - Coding · Asked at: [Palantir](../companies/palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether boundary conditions prevent missing or duplicated records.
